objects.definition:
typedef uint8_t     UINT8;
typedef uint8_t     BYTE;
objects.description: Aliases for an unsigned 8-bit integer type. BYTE is an alternate name for UINT8; both map to uint8_t.

objects.definition: typedef int8_t      INT8;
objects.description: Alias for a signed 8-bit integer type (int8_t).

objects.definition: typedef int         BOOL;
objects.description: Boolean-like integer type. Conventionally 0 is false and non-zero is true. Exact semantics not documented in this header.

objects.definition: typedef uint16_t    UINT16;
objects.description: Alias for an unsigned 16-bit integer type (uint16_t).

objects.definition: typedef int16_t     INT16;
objects.description: Alias for a signed 16-bit integer type (int16_t).

objects.definition: typedef uint32_t    UINT32;
objects.description: Alias for an unsigned 32-bit integer type (uint32_t).

objects.definition: typedef int32_t     INT32;
objects.description: Alias for a signed 32-bit integer type (int32_t).

objects.definition: typedef uint64_t    UINT64;
objects.description: Alias for an unsigned 64-bit integer type (uint64_t).

objects.definition: typedef int64_t     INT64;
objects.description: Alias for a signed 64-bit integer type (int64_t).
Structure describing the TSS2 ABI version components: creator, family, level, and version. Used for runtime ABI negotiation.

objects.definition: typedef uint32_t TSS2_RC;
objects.description: Return code type used by TSS2 APIs. Bit fields encode layer and base error codes as defined by the macros in this header.

objects.definition: typedef UINT16 TPM2_ALG_ID;
objects.description: 16-bit algorithm identifier for TPM 2.0 algorithms. Numerous TPM2_ALG_* constants are defined in this header mapping to numeric IDs.

objects.definition: typedef UINT16                TPM2_ECC_CURVE;
objects.description: 16-bit identifier for supported ECC curves in TPM 2.0. Constants TPM2_ECC_* enumerate curve IDs.

objects.definition: typedef UINT32                                TPM2_CC;
objects.description: 32-bit TPM command code identifier. TPM2_CC_* constants enumerate all commands.

objects.definition: typedef UINT32 TPM2_ALGORITHM_ID;
objects.description: 32-bit legacy (1.2-style) algorithm ID, compatible form of TPM2_ALG_ID.

objects.definition: typedef UINT32 TPM2_MODIFIER_INDICATOR;
objects.description: 32-bit modifier indicator value used by TPM structures; specifics depend on context.

objects.definition: typedef UINT32 TPM2_AUTHORIZATION_SIZE;
objects.description: 32-bit size field for authorization area in TPM commands.

objects.definition: typedef UINT32 TPM2_PARAMETER_SIZE;
objects.description: 32-bit size field for parameter area in TPM commands.

objects.definition: typedef UINT16 TPM2_KEY_SIZE;
objects.description: 16-bit key size in octets.

objects.definition: typedef UINT16 TPM2_KEY_BITS;
objects.description: 16-bit key size in bits for TPM algorithms.

objects.definition: typedef UINT32 TPM2_SPEC;
objects.description: 32-bit spec metadata id. Accompanied by TPM2_SPEC_* constants describing spec family/version info.

objects.definition: typedef UINT32 TPM2_GENERATED;
objects.description: 32-bit magic value used in attestation blobs to indicate TPM-generated structures (TPM2_GENERATED_VALUE).

objects.definition: typedef UINT32 TPM2_RC;
objects.description: 32-bit TPM return code type. Extensive TPM2_RC_* constants define success, error, warning, and formatting info.

objects.definition: typedef INT8 TPM2_CLOCK_ADJUST;
objects.description: Signed 8-bit clock adjustment directive with TPM2_CLOCK_* constants controlling TPM clock rate adjustments.

objects.definition: typedef UINT16 TPM2_EO;
objects.description: 16-bit comparison operation enum used in policies (EQ, NEQ, GT, etc.).

objects.definition: typedef UINT16 TPM2_ST;
objects.description: 16-bit structure tag type. TPM2_ST_* constants identify structure types and command/response tagging.

objects.definition: typedef UINT16 TPM2_SU;
objects.description: 16-bit startup/shutdown type for TPM2_Startup/Shutdown (CLEAR or STATE).

objects.definition: typedef UINT8 TPM2_SE;
objects.description: 8-bit session type identifier (HMAC, POLICY, TRIAL).

objects.definition: typedef UINT32 TPM2_CAP;
objects.description: 32-bit capability selector for TPM2_GetCapability; TPM2_CAP_* constants enumerate capability categories.

objects.definition: typedef UINT32 TPM2_PT;
objects.description: 32-bit TPM property type ID for TPM properties (fixed/variable groups). Numerous TPM2_PT_* constants provided.

objects.definition: typedef UINT32 TPM2_PT_PCR;
objects.description: 32-bit PCR property identifiers for TPM2_PT_PCR_* attributes.

objects.definition: typedef UINT32 TPM2_PS;
objects.description: 32-bit platform-specific indicator for TPM; TPM2_PS_* constants enumerate platform classes.

objects.definition: typedef UINT32 TPM2_HANDLE;
objects.description: Generic 32-bit TPM handle type for objects, sessions, PCRs, NV indices, etc.

objects.definition: typedef UINT8 TPM2_HT;
objects.description: 8-bit handle type indicator defining handle ranges (PCR, NV_INDEX, sessions, etc.).

objects.definition: typedef TPM2_HANDLE TPM2_RH;
objects.description: Alias of TPM2_HANDLE for permanent resource handles; TPM2_RH_* constants enumerate well-known handles.

objects.definition: typedef TPM2_HANDLE TPM2_HC;
objects.description: Alias of TPM2_HANDLE used with range/mask macros to interpret handle spaces (TPM2_HR_*).

objects.definition: typedef uint32_t TPMA_ALGORITHM;
objects.description: Bitfield of algorithm attributes (asymmetric, symmetric, hash, signing, encrypting, method).

objects.definition: typedef uint32_t TPMA_OBJECT;
objects.description: Bitfield of object attributes controlling usage and restrictions of TPM objects.

objects.definition: typedef UINT8 TPMA_SESSION;
objects.description: Bitfield attributes for sessions (continue, auditExclusive, auditReset, decrypt, encrypt, audit).

objects.definition: typedef UINT8 TPMA_LOCALITY;
objects.description: Bitfield for locality assertions (LOC0..LOC4 and extended locality).

objects.definition: typedef uint32_t TPMA_PERMANENT;
objects.description: Bitfield returning TPM permanent state flags (ownerAuthSet, inLockout, etc.).

objects.definition: typedef uint32_t TPMA_STARTUP_CLEAR;
objects.description: Bitfield of TPM flags reset/defined at startup (hierarchy enables, orderly state).

objects.definition: typedef uint32_t TPMA_MEMORY;
objects.description: Bitfield describing TPM memory management characteristics.

objects.definition: typedef uint32_t TPMA_CC;
objects.description: Bitfield describing command attributes (index, NV, extensive, flushed, handle counts).

objects.definition: typedef uint32_t TPMA_MODES;
objects.description: Bitfield of TPM mode indications (e.g., FIPS 140-2).

objects.definition: typedef uint32_t TPMA_X509_KEY_USAGE;
objects.description: Bitfield expressing X.509 keyUsage-mapped requirements for TPM objects.

objects.definition: typedef uint32_t TPMA_ACT;
objects.description: Bitfield for ACT (Authorized Counter Timer) state (signaled, preservesSignaled).

objects.definition: typedef BYTE TPMI_YES_NO;
objects.description: Boolean-like byte type used by TPM interfaces (TPM2_NO/TPM2_YES).

objects.definition: typedef TPM2_HANDLE TPMI_DH_OBJECT;

objects.definition: typedef TPM2_HANDLE TPMI_DH_PARENT;
objects.description: Type alias for a handle identifying a parent object.

objects.definition: typedef TPM2_HANDLE TPMI_DH_PERSISTENT;
objects.description: Alias of handle for persistent object range.

objects.definition: typedef TPM2_HANDLE TPMI_DH_ENTITY;
objects.description: Alias for a handle that may refer to various entity types depending on command.

objects.definition: typedef TPM2_HANDLE TPMI_DH_PCR;
objects.description: Alias for a PCR handle.

objects.definition: typedef TPM2_HANDLE TPMI_SH_AUTH_SESSION;
objects.description: Alias for a session handle used for authorization.

objects.definition: typedef TPM2_HANDLE TPMI_SH_HMAC;
objects.description: Alias for an HMAC session handle.

objects.definition: typedef TPM2_HANDLE TPMI_SH_POLICY;
objects.description: Alias for a policy session handle.

objects.definition: typedef TPM2_HANDLE TPMI_DH_CONTEXT;
objects.description: Alias for a context handle (session/object/sequence contexts).

objects.definition: typedef TPM2_HANDLE TPMI_DH_SAVED;
objects.description: Alias for a saved context type with constants to indicate saved object kind.

objects.definition: typedef TPM2_HANDLE TPMI_RH_HIERARCHY;
objects.description: Alias for a hierarchy handle (owner, endorsement, platform).

objects.definition: typedef TPM2_HANDLE TPMI_RH_ENABLES;
objects.description: Alias for enables handle category.

objects.definition: typedef TPM2_HANDLE TPMI_RH_HIERARCHY_AUTH;
objects.description: Alias for a handle used where hierarchy auth is required.

objects.definition: typedef TPM2_HANDLE TPMI_RH_HIERARCHY_POLICY;
objects.description: Alias for a handle used where hierarchy policy is referenced.

objects.definition: typedef TPM2_HANDLE TPMI_RH_PLATFORM;
objects.description: Alias for platform hierarchy handle.

objects.definition: typedef TPM2_HANDLE TPMI_RH_OWNER;

objects.definition: typedef TPM2_HANDLE TPMI_RH_ENDORSEMENT;

objects.definition: typedef TPM2_HANDLE TPMI_RH_LOCKOUT;

Attestation data for Quote with PCR selection and corresponding digest.
Attestation structure for command audit status and digests.
Attestation structure for session audit info.
Attestation structure for creation data reference (name and hash).
NV certification attestation including contents at an offset.
NV certification attestation using digest of NV contents.

Top-level attestation structure encapsulating attested data and metadata.

Authorization area entry provided with commands for a session.

Aliases for symmetric key sizes (in bits) for AES/SM4/Camellia selectors.

objects.definition: typedef TPM2_ALG_ID TPMI_ALG_KEYEDHASH_SCHEME;

ECC point with X and Y parameters as 2B buffers.

objects.definition:
typedef struct TPMS_ALGORITHM_DETAIL_ECC TPMS_ALGORITHM_DETAIL_ECC;
struct TPMS_ALGORITHM_DETAIL_ECC {
    TPM2_ECC_CURVE      curveID; /* identifier for the curve */
    UINT16              keySize; /* Size in bits of the key */
    TPMT_KDF_SCHEME     kdf;     /* if not TPM2_ALG_NULL the required KDF and hash algorithm used in secret sharing operations */
    TPMT_ECC_SCHEME     sign;    /* If not TPM2_ALG_NULL this is the mandatory signature scheme that is required to be used with this curve. */
    TPM2B_ECC_PARAMETER p;       /* Fp the modulus */
    TPM2B_ECC_PARAMETER a;       /* coefficient of the linear term in the curve equation */
    TPM2B_ECC_PARAMETER b;       /* constant term for curve equation */
    TPM2B_ECC_PARAMETER gX;      /* x coordinate of base point G */
    TPM2B_ECC_PARAMETER gY;      /* y coordinate of base point G */
    TPM2B_ECC_PARAMETER n;       /* order of G */
    TPM2B_ECC_PARAMETER h;       /* cofactor a size of zero indicates a cofactor of 1 */
};
objects.description: Detailed ECC curve domain parameters and associated mandatory schemes.
RSA signature structure parameterized by hash algorithm. Aliased for RSASSA and RSAPSS.
ECC signature containing r and s components and the hash algorithm. Aliased to various ECC schemes.
Union of possible signature representations (RSA, ECC, HMAC, or null).
Tagged signature type carrying actual signature representation.
Opaque container sizes for encrypted secret blobs for ECC, RSA, symmetric, and keyedhash.
2B wrapper for an encrypted secret used in credentialing, duplication, etc.

objects.definition: typedef TPM2_ALG_ID TPMI_ALG_PUBLIC;
objects.description: Alias for public object type selector (keyedhash, symcipher, RSA, ECC).
Union for object unique public identity (key material) depending on type.
Parameters for keyedhash objects (scheme determines capabilities).
Common asymmetric parameter block used in RSA/ECC via TPMU_PUBLIC_PARMS.
RSA-specific public parameters including symmetric companion, RSA scheme, keyBits, exponent.
ECC-specific public parameters including symmetric companion, signing/exchange scheme, curve, and optional KDF.
Union of public parameter sets corresponding to object type.
Tagged set of public parameters used for testing/compat checks.
Public area of a TPM object including type, nameAlg, attributes, policy, parameters, and unique public ID.
2B wrapper for a public area blob used in marshaling/commands.
2B wrapper holding a raw TPMT_PUBLIC template (for e.g., TPM2_CreateLoaded).
Vendor-specific sized buffer used in sensitive composites.
Union of type-specific sensitive materials for TPM objects.
Sensitive area of a TPM object including auth, seed, and type-specific secret material.
2B wrapper for a sensitive area blob (marshaled).
Internal PRIVATE area composition used for TPM2B_PRIVATE encoding (integrities + sensitive).
2B wrapper carrying a marshaled _PRIVATE blob returned/consumed by TPM for private areas.
Identity object used in credential activation containing integrity and encrypted identity fields.
2B wrapper for TPMS_ID_OBJECT bytes.

objects.definition: typedef uint32_t TPM2_NV_INDEX;
objects.description: Packed NV Index handle value with mask/shift macros to extract index and range.

objects.definition: typedef UINT8 TPM2_NT;
objects.description: 8-bit NV Index type identifier with TPM2_NT_* values (ordinary, counter, bits, extend, PIN types).
Parameters returned for PIN counter NV index types indicating current count and limit.

objects.definition: typedef uint32_t TPMA_NV;
objects.description: Bitfield of NV Index attributes controlling access, behavior, and type.
Public description of an NV Index including attributes and policy.
2B wrapper for NV public area.
2B buffer for encrypted sensitive context data.
Context blob payload containing integrity and encrypted sensitive data.
2B wrapper for serialized TPMS_CONTEXT_DATA.
Complete saved context descriptor used for TPM2_ContextSave/Load.
Creation data blob tying a created object to PCR state, locality, parent names, and outside info.
2B wrapper for TPMS_CREATION_DATA.

objects.definition: typedef UINT32 TPM_AT;
objects.description: 32-bit Attached Component tag type for AC capabilities. TPM_AT_* constants enumerate tag meanings.

objects.definition: typedef UINT32 TPM_EA;
objects.description: 32-bit Attached Component event/action code; TPM_AE_NONE defined in this header.
Attached Component capability output record with tag and data.
List of AC capability outputs.
Vendor-specific list of Intel PTT properties guarded by DISABLE_VENDOR macro.

objects.definition: typedef const char *(*TSS2_RC_HANDLER)(TSS2_RC rc);
objects.description: Function pointer type for error/return-code handler callbacks. A handler takes a TSS2_RC and returns a const char* description. Used to plug in custom decoding for specific layers.
Structure describing parsed components of a TSS2 return code. Fields include the originating layer, format, the base error code, and indices for parameter, session, and handle as applicable.

Platform-dependent type used to expose OS polling handles from a TCTI implementation. It aliases to struct pollfd on POSIX-like systems, HANDLE on Windows, void* on Zephyr, and an incomplete void type otherwise (indicating unsupported).

objects.definition: typedef struct TSS2_TCTI_OPAQUE_CONTEXT_BLOB TSS2_TCTI_CONTEXT;
objects.description: Opaque handle type for a TCTI context. The underlying struct is intentionally not defined here; backends define their own layout. Used as the primary handle for transmit/receive/finalize/cancel, etc.

objects.definition:
typedef TSS2_RC (*TSS2_TCTI_TRANSMIT_FCN) (
    TSS2_TCTI_CONTEXT *tctiContext,
    size_t size,
    uint8_t const *command);
objects.description: Function pointer type for TCTI transmit: sends a TPM command buffer to the lower layer.

objects.definition:

    TSS2_TCTI_CONTEXT *tctiContext,

objects.definition:

    TSS2_TCTI_CONTEXT *tctiContext);
objects.description: Function pointer type for TCTI finalize: releases resources for a TCTI context; after this the context is invalid.

objects.definition:

objects.definition:

objects.definition:

Common header layout for TCTI context version 1. TCTI implementations embed or begin with this struct to expose standard function table and metadata (magic/version).
Common header layout for TCTI context version 2, extending V1 with a makeSticky function. Also typedefed as the current common context layout.
Metadata structure describing a TCTI implementation and providing its initialization entry point. Typically returned by a Tss2_Tcti_Info symbol in a provider library.

objects.definition: typedef const TSS2_TCTI_INFO* (*TSS2_TCTI_INFO_FUNC) (void);
objects.description: Function pointer type for retrieving a pointer to a constant TSS2_TCTI_INFO structure (commonly exported as Tss2_Tcti_Info).

Opaque context type for a TCTI (TPM Command Transmission Interface) implementation. It represents the transport/context used by a TCTI module to communicate with a TPM. Only referenced here; definition is provided elsewhere (in tss2_tcti.h or its implementation).
Return code type used by TSS2 APIs. It is referenced here in function prototypes but not defined in this header. No definition present in this file.
Opaque context for a TCTI (TPM Command Transmission Interface). It is only referenced here as a parameter type and not defined in this header.
Standard size type from the C library, referenced as an argument. Not defined in this header.

Opaque TCTI context type referenced by this header but defined elsewhere (in tss2_tcti.h). Used as the transport/context handle for TPM command transmission. Note: not defined in this header; included here only as a referenced parameter type and should be ignored for extraction per instructions.

Opaque TCTI info/metadata type referenced by this header but defined elsewhere (in tss2_tcti.h). Provides module information for a TCTI implementation. Note: not defined in this header; included here only as a referenced parameter type and should be ignored for extraction per instructions.
Return code typedef referenced from tss2_tpm2_types.h; not defined in this header. Note: per instructions, types merely referenced should be ignored.

objects.definition: typedef struct _TSS2_SYS_OPAQUE_CONTEXT_BLOB TSS2_SYS_CONTEXT;
objects.description: Opaque SAPI (System API) context handle used by the TSS System API. The actual struct is intentionally not defined here; callers treat it as an opaque handle passed to all Tss2_Sys_* functions.

objects.definition: typedef uint32_t ESYS_TR;

objects.definition: typedef struct ESYS_CONTEXT ESYS_CONTEXT;
objects.description: Forward-declared opaque ESAPI context object managing connection state to a TPM via a TCTI, session tracking, transient handle mapping, and command dispatch. Actual structure is private to the library.

objects.definition: typedef struct ESYS_CRYPTO_CONTEXT_BLOB ESYS_CRYPTO_CONTEXT_BLOB;
objects.description: Forward-declared opaque blob used by pluggable crypto callbacks to hold per-operation state for hash and HMAC computations (and reused across various crypto ops). Implementation is backend-specific and not defined in this header.

objects.definition:
typedef TSS2_RC
    (*ESYS_CRYPTO_HASH_START_FNP)(

functions.name: Tss2_RC_Decode
functions.signature: const char *Tss2_RC_Decode(TSS2_RC rc);
functions.description: Decode a TPM2-TSS TSS2_RC return code into a human-readable string. Typically used for logging or diagnostics to turn a numeric TSS2_RC into a message. The returned string is intended to describe the rc value (including, if known, the layer and specific error). Additional details (format, parameter/session/handle selector) are not included; use Tss2_RC_DecodeInfo for structured breakdown.
requirements: Argument rc may be any valid TSS2_RC value (unknown specifics of valid range depend on tss2_tpm2_types.h).
The returned const char* points to memory that must not be modified by the caller (inferred from const).
Ownership of the returned string is not transferred; do not free it (inferred from const char* return).

functions.name: Tss2_RC_SetHandler
functions.signature: TSS2_RC_HANDLER Tss2_RC_SetHandler(uint8_t layer, const char *name, TSS2_RC_HANDLER handler);
functions.description: Install or replace a custom decoding handler for a specific layer of TSS2_RC values. The handler is a callback of type TSS2_RC_HANDLER (const char *(*)(TSS2_RC)) used to produce human-readable text for error codes belonging to the given layer, optionally associated with the provided name. Returns a TSS2_RC_HANDLER (likely the previous handler) to allow restoration, though exact semantics are not documented here.
requirements: Argument layer is an 8-bit value selecting the layer (0–255) (type-based inference).
Argument name should be a valid C string pointer if provided; exact usage and lifetime requirements are unknown (not documented).
Argument handler must be a valid function pointer of type const char *(*)(TSS2_RC) if provided; whether NULL unsets a handler is unknown (not documented).
The returned TSS2_RC_HANDLER may be NULL if no previous handler exists; exact behavior is unknown (not documented).

functions.name: Tss2_RC_DecodeInfo
functions.signature: TSS2_RC Tss2_RC_DecodeInfo(TSS2_RC rc, TSS2_RC_INFO *info);
functions.description: Decode a TSS2_RC into structured components in a TSS2_RC_INFO struct (layer, format, base error, and selector fields: parameter, session, handle). This provides machine-usable details about the error composition. Returns a TSS2_RC status code indicating the outcome (exact success/error values are not documented here).
requirements: Argument info must be a non-NULL pointer to writable storage for a TSS2_RC_INFO structure; the function writes decoded fields into it (pointer validity inferred from output parameter).
Argument rc may be any TSS2_RC to decode; specifics of valid ranges are defined by tss2_tpm2_types.h (unknown here).
Callers should not assume info is initialized prior to the call; the function is expected to populate it (inferred).
Interpretation of the return value (success vs. failure code) is not specified in this header and must be checked against the library’s conventions (unknown here).

functions.name: Tss2_RC_DecodeInfoError
functions.signature: const char *Tss2_RC_DecodeInfoError(TSS2_RC_INFO *info);
functions.description: Return a human-readable string describing the error indicated by a previously decoded TSS2_RC_INFO structure. Use after Tss2_RC_DecodeInfo to obtain a text explanation that respects the decoded format and selector fields.
requirements: Argument info must be a non-NULL pointer to a TSS2_RC_INFO structure that has been filled by a successful call to Tss2_RC_DecodeInfo (inferred from usage).
The returned const char* must not be modified or freed by the caller (inferred from const).

functions.name: Tss2_Tcti_Transmit
functions.signature: TSS2_RC Tss2_Tcti_Transmit(TSS2_TCTI_CONTEXT *tctiContext, size_t size, const uint8_t *command)
functions.description: Macro wrapper that invokes the TCTI transport’s transmit callback to send a TPM command buffer. Use this to submit a prepared TPM2 command of length size bytes over the selected TCTI (device, socket, etc.). Returns a TSS2_RC indicating success or the specific error code produced by the TCTI.
requirements: tctiContext must be a valid, initialized TSS2_TCTI_CONTEXT whose version is >= 1 (macro returns TSS2_TCTI_RC_ABI_MISMATCH otherwise).
The transmit function pointer in the context must be non-NULL (macro returns TSS2_TCTI_RC_NOT_IMPLEMENTED otherwise).
command must point to a readable buffer of at least size bytes; size must describe the exact number of bytes to send.
If tctiContext is NULL, the macro returns TSS2_TCTI_RC_BAD_REFERENCE.

functions.name: Tss2_Tcti_Receive
functions.signature: TSS2_RC Tss2_Tcti_Receive(TSS2_TCTI_CONTEXT *tctiContext, size_t *size, uint8_t *response, int32_t timeout)
functions.description: Macro wrapper that invokes the TCTI transport’s receive callback to obtain a TPM response buffer. Typically called after Tss2_Tcti_Transmit. The timeout controls blocking behavior (see timeout constants). Returns a TSS2_RC from the TCTI layer.
requirements: tctiContext must be a valid, initialized TSS2_TCTI_CONTEXT whose version is >= 1 (macro returns TSS2_TCTI_RC_ABI_MISMATCH otherwise).
The receive function pointer in the context must be non-NULL (macro returns TSS2_TCTI_RC_NOT_IMPLEMENTED otherwise).
size must be a valid pointer; the underlying TCTI uses it for buffer length in/out.
response must point to a writable buffer of at least *size bytes unless the specific TCTI documents a size-query pattern; this header does not define such behavior.
timeout is an int32_t controlling wait semantics; TSS2_TCTI_TIMEOUT_BLOCK (-1) for blocking and TSS2_TCTI_TIMEOUT_NONE (0) for non-blocking are defined constants.
If tctiContext is NULL, the macro returns TSS2_TCTI_RC_BAD_REFERENCE.

functions.name: Tss2_Tcti_Finalize
functions.signature: void Tss2_Tcti_Finalize(TSS2_TCTI_CONTEXT *tctiContext)
functions.description: Macro that conditionally invokes the TCTI transport’s finalize callback to tear down and release resources for the TCTI context. Safe to call on NULL or on contexts lacking a finalize method (it becomes a no-op).
requirements: If tctiContext is not NULL, it must be an initialized TSS2_TCTI_CONTEXT with version >= 1 for finalize to be called.
If tctiContext is NULL, or version < 1, or finalize is NULL, the macro performs no operation.
After a successful finalize, the context is no longer valid for further TCTI calls.

functions.name: Tss2_Tcti_Cancel
functions.signature: TSS2_RC Tss2_Tcti_Cancel(TSS2_TCTI_CONTEXT *tctiContext)
functions.description: Macro wrapper that invokes the TCTI transport’s cancel callback to attempt to cancel an in-flight TPM command if supported by the transport. Returns a TSS2_RC.
requirements: tctiContext must be a valid, initialized TSS2_TCTI_CONTEXT whose version is >= 1 (macro returns TSS2_TCTI_RC_ABI_MISMATCH otherwise).
The cancel function pointer in the context must be non-NULL (macro returns TSS2_TCTI_RC_NOT_IMPLEMENTED otherwise).
If tctiContext is NULL, the macro returns TSS2_TCTI_RC_BAD_REFERENCE.

functions.name: Tss2_Tcti_GetPollHandles
functions.signature: TSS2_RC Tss2_Tcti_GetPollHandles(TSS2_TCTI_CONTEXT *tctiContext, TSS2_TCTI_POLL_HANDLE *handles, size_t *num_handles)
functions.description: Macro wrapper that invokes the TCTI transport’s getPollHandles callback to obtain OS-specific poll/select handles for integration into event loops. Returns a TSS2_RC.
requirements: tctiContext must be a valid, initialized TSS2_TCTI_CONTEXT whose version is >= 1 (macro returns TSS2_TCTI_RC_ABI_MISMATCH otherwise).
The getPollHandles function pointer in the context must be non-NULL (macro returns TSS2_TCTI_RC_NOT_IMPLEMENTED otherwise).

handles (if provided) must reference writable storage for at least *num_handles entries of TSS2_TCTI_POLL_HANDLE; actual usage pattern (e.g., query vs. fill) is implementation-defined and not specified here.
num_handles must be a valid pointer.
If tctiContext is NULL, the macro returns TSS2_TCTI_RC_BAD_REFERENCE.

functions.name: Tss2_Tcti_SetLocality
functions.signature: TSS2_RC Tss2_Tcti_SetLocality(TSS2_TCTI_CONTEXT *tctiContext, uint8_t locality)
functions.description: Macro wrapper that invokes the TCTI transport’s setLocality callback to request a TPM locality change for subsequent commands. Returns a TSS2_RC.
requirements: tctiContext must be a valid, initialized TSS2_TCTI_CONTEXT whose version is >= 1 (macro returns TSS2_TCTI_RC_ABI_MISMATCH otherwise).
The setLocality function pointer in the context must be non-NULL (macro returns TSS2_TCTI_RC_NOT_IMPLEMENTED otherwise).
locality is an 8-bit value; valid range is implementation-defined by the TCTI/TPM platform (commonly 0–4 for TPM2), not specified in this header.
If tctiContext is NULL, the macro returns TSS2_TCTI_RC_BAD_REFERENCE.

functions.name: Tss2_Tcti_MakeSticky
functions.signature: TSS2_RC Tss2_Tcti_MakeSticky(TSS2_TCTI_CONTEXT *tctiContext, TPM2_HANDLE *handle, uint8_t sticky)
functions.description: Macro wrapper that invokes the TCTI transport’s makeSticky callback (available in version >= 2 contexts) to set or clear the ‘sticky’ attribute on a TPM handle if supported by the transport/platform. Returns a TSS2_RC.
requirements: tctiContext must be a valid, initialized TSS2_TCTI_CONTEXT whose version is >= 2 (macro returns TSS2_TCTI_RC_ABI_MISMATCH otherwise).
The makeSticky function pointer in the context must be non-NULL (macro returns TSS2_TCTI_RC_NOT_IMPLEMENTED otherwise).
handle must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to a TPM2_HANDLE value; whether the handle is modified by the call is implementation-specific and not defined here.
sticky is an 8-bit flag; semantics (e.g., 0 = clear, 1 = set) are implementation-defined and not specified in this header.
If tctiContext is NULL, the macro returns TSS2_TCTI_RC_BAD_REFERENCE.

functions.name: Tss2_Tcti_Info
functions.signature: const TSS2_TCTI_INFO* Tss2_Tcti_Info(void)
functions.description: Factory/metadata function symbol exported by a TCTI provider that returns a pointer to a TSS2_TCTI_INFO describing the implementation (version, name, description, config_help, and init function). The symbol name is provided by TSS2_TCTI_INFO_SYMBOL ("Tss2_Tcti_Info") for dynamic loading. Typical usage: dlsym/GetProcAddress this symbol from a TCTI module and call it to obtain the init entry point and metadata.
requirements: Callable with no arguments and returns a non-NULL pointer on success; NULL return handling is implementation-defined (not specified here).
When dynamically loading, resolve the symbol name given by TSS2_TCTI_INFO_SYMBOL.
The returned TSS2_TCTI_INFO->init must be used to initialize a TCTI context before using the Tcti macros/callbacks in this header.

functions.name: Tss2_Tcti_Device_Init
functions.signature: TSS2_RC Tss2_Tcti_Device_Init(TSS2_TCTI_CONTEXT *tctiContext, size_t *size, const char *conf);
functions.description: Initializes a TSS2 TCTI context for communicating with a TPM via the "device" TCTI (typically a system TPM device such as /dev/tpm0 or /dev/tpmrm0). Usual usage follows a two-step pattern: first call with tctiContext == NULL to obtain the required context size via *size, then allocate a buffer of that size and call again with tctiContext pointing to the buffer to perform initialization. The conf parameter is an optional, null-terminated configuration string (implementation-specific; often used to select the device path). Returns a TSS2_RC status code indicating success or the reason for failure.
requirements: If querying the required context size, pass tctiContext == NULL and a non-NULL size pointer; on return *size will contain the number of bytes required for the TCTI context (exact return-code semantics are implementation-specific).
If performing initialization, tctiContext must point to a writable buffer of at least *size bytes (as obtained from a prior size query) and size must be non-NULL.
conf, if provided, must be a valid, null-terminated C string; if NULL, implementation-defined defaults are used (exact supported options/format are unknown from this header).
The returned TCTI context must be successfully initialized before it is used with higher-level TSS2 APIs (e.g., Tss2_Sys_Initialize).
Callers must check the returned TSS2_RC and handle errors appropriately; no exceptions are thrown.
Thread-safety or reentrancy guarantees are not specified here; perform initialization before concurrent use.
Resource management and finalization of the TCTI context are not defined in this header; follow the library’s documented shutdown/cleanup procedure (unknown from this header).

functions.name: tcti_platform_command
functions.signature: TSS2_RC tcti_platform_command(TSS2_TCTI_CONTEXT *tctiContext, UINT32 cmd);
functions.description: Sends an out-of-band platform command to a TPM simulator via the TCTI (MSSIM) “other socket”. Typical usage is to control simulator state (e.g., power on/off, cancel on/off, NV on) or to end a simulator TPM session using the provided MS_SIM_* and TPM_SESSION_END command codes. Returns a TSS2_RC status code indicating success or failure. Exact side effects and additional data paths are not described here and may depend on the simulator implementation.
requirements: tctiContext must point to a valid, initialized TSS2_TCTI_CONTEXT associated with the MSSIM TCTI before calling.

cmd should be one of the defined command codes: MS_SIM_POWER_ON (1), MS_SIM_POWER_OFF (2), MS_SIM_TPM_SEND_COMMAND (8), MS_SIM_CANCEL_ON (9), MS_SIM_CANCEL_OFF (10), MS_SIM_NV_ON (11), or TPM_SESSION_END (20); other values may be rejected or undefined.
Caller must handle the returned TSS2_RC error code appropriately (non-success indicates failure).
Function may perform network/socket I/O; ensure the environment permits communication with the simulator’s out-of-band channel.

functions.name: Tss2_Tcti_Mssim_Init
functions.signature: TSS2_RC Tss2_Tcti_Mssim_Init(TSS2_TCTI_CONTEXT *tctiContext, size_t *size, const char *conf);
functions.description: Initializes a TCTI context for the TPM simulator (MSSIM). Typical two-step usage: first call with tctiContext == NULL to query and store the required context size in *size; then allocate a buffer of that size and call again with tctiContext pointing to it to complete initialization. The conf string provides simulator connection parameters (format is implementation-defined; commonly host/port values). Returns a TSS2_RC status code.
requirements: If tctiContext is NULL, size must be non-NULL; on return, *size receives the required context size (sizing query pattern).
If tctiContext is non-NULL, it must point to a writable buffer of at least *size bytes, and size must be non-NULL and set to the buffer size.
conf must be a valid pointer to a configuration string expected by the MSSIM TCTI, or NULL if the implementation allows it (exact format is not specified here).
Caller must check the returned TSS2_RC and not use the context if initialization fails.
This function must be called before using the TCTI context with higher-level TPM2-TSS APIs.

functions.name: Tss2_Tcti_Swtpm_Init
functions.signature:
TSS2_RC Tss2_Tcti_Swtpm_Init(
    TSS2_TCTI_CONTEXT *tctiContext,
    size_t *size,
    const char *conf);
functions.description: Initializes a TCTI (TPM Command Transmission Interface) context that communicates with an swtpm (software TPM) instance. Typical TCTI init semantics apply: when tctiContext is NULL, the function writes the required context size to *size; when tctiContext is non-NULL, it initializes the caller-provided memory using the configuration string. Use this to create a transport layer for SAPI/ESAPI TPM calls targeting swtpm. Specific configuration keys for conf are not documented in this header; implementations commonly accept a NULL or NUL-terminated string with backend-specific options.
requirements: If tctiContext == NULL, size MUST be non-NULL and will be set to the number of bytes required for the TCTI context.
If tctiContext != NULL, size MUST be non-NULL and *size MUST be at least the number of bytes previously indicated by an initial sizing call.
When tctiContext != NULL, tctiContext MUST point to writable memory of at least *size bytes and be suitably aligned for TSS2_TCTI_CONTEXT.
conf MAY be NULL or a NUL-terminated configuration string; specific key/value format is backend-defined and not specified here.
Must be successfully called before any other TCTI operations are performed on this context.
Do not re-initialize an already initialized context without finalizing/closing it via the appropriate TCTI finalize/close routine from tss2_tcti.h.
Return code is a TSS2_RC; callers MUST check for TSS2_RC_SUCCESS before using the context.

functions.name: Tss2_Tcti_Swtpm_Reset
functions.signature:
TSS2_RC Tss2_Tcti_Swtpm_Reset(
    TSS2_TCTI_CONTEXT *tctiContext);
functions.description: Resets the swtpm TCTI context/connection. Intended to re-establish or clear the transport state associated with an existing swtpm-backed TCTI context. Exact reset semantics (e.g., whether TPM state is affected or only the transport) are not documented in this header and may be implementation-defined.
requirements: tctiContext MUST be a valid, previously initialized TSS2_TCTI_CONTEXT created by Tss2_Tcti_Swtpm_Init.
tctiContext MUST NOT be NULL.
Callers MUST check the returned TSS2_RC and treat non-success as a failure to reset.
Concurrency requirements are unspecified; to be safe, do not call concurrently with in-flight TCTI operations on the same context.
Post-reset state expectations beyond a successful return are implementation-defined; callers SHOULD be prepared to re-send commands as needed.

functions.name: Tss2_TctiLdr_Finalize
functions.signature: void Tss2_TctiLdr_Finalize(TSS2_TCTI_CONTEXT **context);
functions.description: Shuts down and releases a TCTI context previously created by the TCTI loader, given by a pointer-to-pointer to TSS2_TCTI_CONTEXT. Intended to be called during teardown to free resources associated with the loaded TCTI. It likely invalidates the context and may set the pointer to NULL, but exact postconditions are not specified in this header.
requirements: context must be a valid, non-null pointer to a TSS2_TCTI_CONTEXT*
*context should point to a valid TCTI context obtained via Tss2_TctiLdr_Initialize or Tss2_TctiLdr_Initialize_Ex
Do not use the TCTI context after finalization
Thread-safety and reentrancy are unknown; avoid concurrent use of the same context pointer during finalization

functions.name: Tss2_TctiLdr_Initialize_Ex
functions.signature: TSS2_RC Tss2_TctiLdr_Initialize_Ex(const char *name, const char *conf, TSS2_TCTI_CONTEXT **context);
functions.description: Loads and initializes a TPM Command Transmission Interface (TCTI) implementation by name with an optional configuration string, returning an initialized TSS2_TCTI_CONTEXT via output parameter. Use this to select a specific TCTI (e.g., device, mssim) and pass backend-specific configuration. Returns a TSS2_RC status that the caller must check.
requirements: name, if non-null, must be a null-terminated C string naming a TCTI implementation
conf, if non-null, must be a null-terminated C string with TCTI-specific configuration
context must be a valid, non-null pointer to a TSS2_TCTI_CONTEXT* to receive the initialized context
On success, the caller owns the returned context and must later call Tss2_TctiLdr_Finalize to release it
Caller must check the returned TSS2_RC and only use *context on success
Behavior for NULL name or conf is library-defined and not specified here; treat as unknown
Thread-safety and multiple initializations are not specified; avoid sharing the same output pointer across threads

functions.name: Tss2_TctiLdr_Initialize
functions.signature: TSS2_RC Tss2_TctiLdr_Initialize(const char *nameConf, TSS2_TCTI_CONTEXT **context);
functions.description: Loads and initializes a TCTI using a single string that encodes both the TCTI name and its configuration (commonly in the form "name:conf"), returning an initialized TSS2_TCTI_CONTEXT via output parameter. Use this convenience API when providing combined name/config input. Returns a TSS2_RC that must be checked.
requirements: nameConf, if non-null, must be a null-terminated C string that specifies the TCTI and configuration in an implementation-defined format
context must be a valid, non-null pointer to a TSS2_TCTI_CONTEXT* to receive the initialized context
On success, the caller owns the returned context and must later call Tss2_TctiLdr_Finalize to release it
Caller must check the returned TSS2_RC and only use *context on success
Exact format of nameConf, default behavior for NULL, and supported schemes are not specified here; treat as unknown
Avoid concurrent use of the same output pointer across threads

functions.name: Tss2_TctiLdr_GetInfo
functions.signature: TSS2_RC Tss2_TctiLdr_GetInfo(const char *name, TSS2_TCTI_INFO **info);
functions.description: Retrieves a TCTI information structure for the named TCTI implementation without instantiating a context. Use to query metadata (e.g., description, init function pointer) about a TCTI before initialization. The returned info must be freed with Tss2_TctiLdr_FreeInfo. Returns a TSS2_RC status that must be checked.
requirements: name must be a non-null, null-terminated C string naming a TCTI implementation (NULL handling is not specified; treat as unknown)
info must be a valid, non-null pointer to a TSS2_TCTI_INFO* to receive the result
On success, *info will refer to an allocated TSS2_TCTI_INFO that the caller must later free with Tss2_TctiLdr_FreeInfo
Caller must check the returned TSS2_RC and only use *info on success
Do not pass *info from one loader/free pair to another library; only free with Tss2_TctiLdr_FreeInfo

functions.name: Tss2_TctiLdr_FreeInfo
functions.signature: void Tss2_TctiLdr_FreeInfo(TSS2_TCTI_INFO **info);
functions.description: Frees a TCTI information structure previously returned by Tss2_TctiLdr_GetInfo. Intended for releasing loader-allocated metadata resources. After freeing, the info pointer may be invalidated or set to NULL (unspecified here).
requirements: info must be a valid, non-null pointer to a TSS2_TCTI_INFO*
*info should be a value previously obtained from Tss2_TctiLdr_GetInfo
Do not use the info object after it has been freed
Thread-safety is unspecified; avoid freeing the same info concurrently

functions.name: Tss2_Sys_GetContextSize
functions.signature: size_t Tss2_Sys_GetContextSize(size_t maxCommandResponseSize);
functions.description: Returns the number of bytes required to allocate a TSS2_SYS_CONTEXT capable of handling a given maximum TPM command/response size. Used prior to Initialize to allocate the context buffer.
requirements: maxCommandResponseSize must be a non-zero size large enough for the target TPM/TCTI maximum transmit/receive size.
Caller must use the returned size to allocate the buffer for TSS2_SYS_CONTEXT and pass that same size to Tss2_Sys_Initialize.

functions.name: Tss2_Sys_Initialize
functions.signature: TSS2_RC Tss2_Sys_Initialize(TSS2_SYS_CONTEXT *sysContext, size_t contextSize, TSS2_TCTI_CONTEXT *tctiContext, TSS2_ABI_VERSION *abiVersion);
functions.description: Initializes a SAPI system context over a provided memory buffer and an already-initialized TCTI context. Optionally returns or validates ABI version.
requirements: sysContext must point to a caller-allocated buffer of at least contextSize bytes, typically obtained via Tss2_Sys_GetContextSize.
contextSize must match the buffer size and be compatible with maxCommandResponseSize used for sizing.
tctiContext must be a valid, initialized TCTI transport context.
abiVersion may be NULL or point to a valid structure; if non-NULL, fields must be set/checked per implementation expectations.
Must be called before any other Tss2_Sys_* operations on sysContext.
Returns TSS2_RC error codes; caller must check and not use sysContext on failure.

functions.name: Tss2_Sys_Finalize
functions.signature: void Tss2_Sys_Finalize(TSS2_SYS_CONTEXT *sysContext);
functions.description: Finalizes and invalidates a previously initialized system API context. Releases any internal associations with the TCTI; does not free caller memory.
requirements: sysContext must be a valid context previously initialized by Tss2_Sys_Initialize.
After finalize, the context must not be used unless re-initialized.
Caller remains responsible for freeing the memory buffer if dynamically allocated.

functions.name: Tss2_Sys_GetTctiContext
functions.signature: TSS2_RC Tss2_Sys_GetTctiContext(TSS2_SYS_CONTEXT *sysContext, TSS2_TCTI_CONTEXT **tctiContext);
functions.description: Retrieves the TCTI context associated with a system context.
requirements: sysContext must be a valid initialized SAPI context.
tctiContext must be a non-NULL output pointer to receive the TCTI context.
Caller must check the returned TSS2_RC before using the output pointer.

functions.name: Tss2_Sys_GetDecryptParam
functions.signature: TSS2_RC Tss2_Sys_GetDecryptParam(TSS2_SYS_CONTEXT *sysContext, size_t *decryptParamSize, const uint8_t **decryptParamBuffer);
functions.description: Obtains a pointer and size to the current command’s decrypt parameter buffer prepared in sysContext (for parameter encryption/decryption handling).
requirements: sysContext must be a valid initialized context with a command prepared that supports a decrypt parameter.
decryptParamSize and decryptParamBuffer must be non-NULL output pointers.
Returned buffer pointer is owned by sysContext and valid until command re-preparation or context reuse.

functions.name: Tss2_Sys_SetDecryptParam
functions.signature: TSS2_RC Tss2_Sys_SetDecryptParam(TSS2_SYS_CONTEXT *sysContext, size_t decryptParamSize, const uint8_t *decryptParamBuffer);
functions.description: Sets/overrides the command decrypt parameter bytes in the prepared command buffer for parameter encryption/decryption processing.
requirements: sysContext must be valid and have a command prepared that supports a decrypt parameter.
If decryptParamSize > 0 then decryptParamBuffer must be non-NULL and point to at least decryptParamSize bytes.
The size must conform to the command’s expected parameter bounds; the function returns an error if invalid.

functions.name: Tss2_Sys_GetCpBuffer
functions.signature: TSS2_RC Tss2_Sys_GetCpBuffer(TSS2_SYS_CONTEXT *sysContext, size_t *cpBufferUsedSize, const uint8_t **cpBuffer);
functions.description: Returns the raw command parameter (cp) buffer and size from the prepared command currently in sysContext.
requirements: sysContext must be a valid initialized context with a prepared command.
cpBufferUsedSize and cpBuffer must be non-NULL output pointers.
Returned buffer is internal to sysContext and read-only/ephemeral.

functions.name: Tss2_Sys_SetCmdAuths
functions.signature: TSS2_RC Tss2_Sys_SetCmdAuths(TSS2_SYS_CONTEXT *sysContext, const TSS2L_SYS_AUTH_COMMAND *cmdAuthsArray);
functions.description: Associates one or more authorization structures with the next command execution in sysContext.
requirements: sysContext must be initialized and have a command prepared (or will be used for the next Execute).
cmdAuthsArray may be NULL to indicate no authorizations or must point to a properly populated list with count <= TSS2_SYS_MAX_SESSIONS.
Each TPMS_AUTH_COMMAND entry must be correctly initialized (session handles, nonces, attributes, HMAC sizes).

functions.name: Tss2_Sys_ExecuteAsync
functions.signature: TSS2_RC Tss2_Sys_ExecuteAsync(TSS2_SYS_CONTEXT *sysContext);
functions.description: Submits the currently prepared command (with any set auths) to the TPM asynchronously through the TCTI.
requirements: sysContext must be initialized and have a command prepared.
Command authorizations/parameters must have been set before calling.
Caller must subsequently call Tss2_Sys_ExecuteFinish to complete the transaction.
Not all TCTIs support async; errors may be returned accordingly.

functions.name: Tss2_Sys_ExecuteFinish
functions.signature: TSS2_RC Tss2_Sys_ExecuteFinish(TSS2_SYS_CONTEXT *sysContext, int32_t timeout);
functions.description: Completes an asynchronous command execution, receiving the TPM response. Supports timeout semantics as defined by the TCTI.
requirements: sysContext must be initialized and in a state where ExecuteAsync was called.
timeout dictates wait behavior (implementation-defined; often -1 for infinite).
Caller must provide storage for any response data via subsequent completion helpers or by parsing response in sysContext.
Return code must be checked; on error the internal state may be reset.

functions.name: Tss2_Sys_Execute
functions.signature: TSS2_RC Tss2_Sys_Execute(TSS2_SYS_CONTEXT *sysContext);
functions.description: Convenience synchronous execution: transmits the prepared command and waits for completion, populating internal response buffers.
requirements: sysContext must be initialized with a prepared command and optional auths set.
Caller must retrieve response data via appropriate Get* or _Complete helpers after success.
Return code must be checked.

functions.name: Tss2_Sys_GetCommandCode
functions.signature: TSS2_RC Tss2_Sys_GetCommandCode(TSS2_SYS_CONTEXT *sysContext, UINT8 *commandCode);
functions.description: Retrieves the TPM command code byte/identifier of the prepared or last executed command in sysContext.
requirements: sysContext must be initialized; typically a command should be prepared or executed.
commandCode must be a non-NULL output pointer.

functions.name: Tss2_Sys_GetRspAuths
functions.signature: TSS2_RC Tss2_Sys_GetRspAuths(TSS2_SYS_CONTEXT *sysContext, TSS2L_SYS_AUTH_RESPONSE *rspAuthsArray);
functions.description: Retrieves the response authorization area parsed from the last TPM response.
requirements: sysContext must be initialized and have a completed command with response auths.
rspAuthsArray must be a valid output structure pointer to receive parsed auths.

functions.name: Tss2_Sys_GetEncryptParam
functions.signature: TSS2_RC Tss2_Sys_GetEncryptParam(TSS2_SYS_CONTEXT *sysContext, size_t *encryptParamSize, const uint8_t **encryptParamBuffer);
functions.description: Provides size and pointer to the response encrypt parameter from the last TPM response (used for parameter encryption).
requirements: sysContext must be initialized and have a completed command with an encrypt parameter in its response.
encryptParamSize and encryptParamBuffer must be non-NULL output pointers.
Returned pointer is owned by sysContext and is transient.

functions.name: Tss2_Sys_SetEncryptParam
functions.signature: TSS2_RC Tss2_Sys_SetEncryptParam(TSS2_SYS_CONTEXT *sysContext, size_t encryptParamSize, const uint8_t *encryptParamBuffer);
functions.description: Overrides/sets the response encrypt parameter bytes in sysContext prior to HMAC calculation/verification steps where applicable.
requirements: sysContext must be initialized and in a state expecting an encrypt parameter.
If encryptParamSize > 0, encryptParamBuffer must be non-NULL and at least encryptParamSize bytes.
Size must match expected parameter bounds for the command.

functions.name: Tss2_Sys_GetRpBuffer
functions.signature: TSS2_RC Tss2_Sys_GetRpBuffer(TSS2_SYS_CONTEXT *sysContext, size_t *rpBufferUsedSize, const uint8_t **rpBuffer);
functions.description: Returns the raw response parameter (rp) buffer and size for the last executed command.
requirements: sysContext must be initialized and have a completed command.
rpBufferUsedSize and rpBuffer must be non-NULL output pointers.
Returned pointer is internal to sysContext and read-only/temporary.

functions.name: Tss2_Sys_Startup_Prepare
functions.signature: TSS2_RC Tss2_Sys_Startup_Prepare(TSS2_SYS_CONTEXT *sysContext, TPM2_SU startupType);
functions.description: Prepares a TPM2_Startup command with the given startup type in sysContext (no transmission).
requirements: sysContext must be initialized.
startupType must be a valid TPM2_SU enum value.

functions.name: Tss2_Sys_Startup_Complete
functions.signature: TSS2_RC Tss2_Sys_Startup_Complete(TSS2_SYS_CONTEXT *sysContext);
functions.description: Parses/finishes a TPM2_Startup command after execution, consuming the response and updating internal state.
requirements: sysContext must be initialized and have executed the prepared Startup command successfully before calling Complete.

functions.name: Tss2_Sys_Startup
functions.signature: TSS2_RC Tss2_Sys_Startup(TSS2_SYS_CONTEXT *sysContext, TPM2_SU startupType);
functions.description: Convenience wrapper that prepares and executes TPM2_Startup with the provided type synchronously.
requirements: sysContext must be initialized.
startupType must be a valid TPM2_SU value.
Caller must check TSS2_RC for success.

functions.name: Tss2_Sys_Shutdown_Prepare
functions.signature: TSS2_RC Tss2_Sys_Shutdown_Prepare(TSS2_SYS_CONTEXT *sysContext, TPM2_SU shutdownType);
functions.description: Prepares a TPM2_Shutdown command with the specified shutdown type.
requirements: sysContext must be initialized.
shutdownType must be a valid TPM2_SU.

functions.name: Tss2_Sys_Shutdown_Complete

functions.name: Tss2_Sys_Create_Prepare

functions.name: Tss2_Sys_Create_Complete
functions.signature: TSS2_RC Tss2_Sys_Create_Complete(TSS2_SYS_CONTEXT *sysContext, TPM2B_PRIVATE *outPrivate, TPM2B_PUBLIC *outPublic, TPM2B_CREATION_DATA *creationData, TPM2B_DIGEST *creationHash, TPMT_TK_CREATION *creationTicket);
functions.description: Completes TPM2_Create, returning private/public areas and creation data/hash/ticket.

functions.description: Executes TPM2_Create synchronously to produce a new child object’s blobs and creation artifacts.

functions.description: Executes TPM2_LoadExternal synchronously to import an external object and returns handle/name.

cmdAuthsArray and rspAuthsArray may be NULL or valid.

functions.description: Executes TPM2_ReadPublic synchronously, returning public info and names for an object.

functions.description: Completes TPM2_ActivateCredential and returns the decrypted credential digest.

functions.name: Tss2_Sys_ActivateCredential
functions.signature: TSS2_RC Tss2_Sys_ActivateCredential(TSS2_SYS_CONTEXT *sysContext, TPMI_DH_OBJECT activateHandle, TPMI_DH_OBJECT keyHandle, TSS2L_SYS_AUTH_COMMAND const *cmdAuthsArray, const TPM2B_ID_OBJECT *credentialBlob, const TPM2B_ENCRYPTED_SECRET *secret, TPM2B_DIGEST *certInfo, TSS2L_SYS_AUTH_RESPONSE *rspAuthsArray);
functions.description: Executes TPM2_ActivateCredential synchronously to recover a credential digest using provided handles and blobs.

cmdAuthsArray and rspAuthsArray may be NULL or valid pointers.

functions.description: Executes TPM2_MakeCredential synchronously, producing a credential blob and encrypted secret for a named object.

cmdAuthsArray and rspAuthsArray may be NULL or valid.

functions.description: Completes TPM2_Unseal and outputs the unsealed data.

functions.name: Tss2_Sys_Unseal
functions.signature: TSS2_RC Tss2_Sys_Unseal(TSS2_SYS_CONTEXT *sysContext, TPMI_DH_OBJECT itemHandle, TSS2L_SYS_AUTH_COMMAND const *cmdAuthsArray, TPM2B_SENSITIVE_DATA *outData, TSS2L_SYS_AUTH_RESPONSE *rspAuthsArray);
functions.description: Executes TPM2_Unseal synchronously, returning the unsealed sensitive data.

functions.name: Tss2_Sys_ObjectChangeAuth_Prepare

newAuth must point to a valid TPM2B_AUTH structure
objectHandle and parentHandle must be valid TPM handles appropriate for ObjectChangeAuth
Call ExecuteAsync/Execute (or ExecuteFinish after Async) after Prepare before calling the corresponding Complete

functions.name: Tss2_Sys_ObjectChangeAuth_Complete
functions.signature: TSS2_RC Tss2_Sys_ObjectChangeAuth_Complete(TSS2_SYS_CONTEXT *sysContext, TPM2B_PRIVATE *outPrivate);

requirements: sysContext must be the same context used for Prepare/Execute of this command
outPrivate must be a valid pointer to receive the TPM2B_PRIVATE result
Must be called only after a successful Execute* of the corresponding Prepare

functions.name: Tss2_Sys_ObjectChangeAuth
functions.signature: TSS2_RC Tss2_Sys_ObjectChangeAuth(TSS2_SYS_CONTEXT *sysContext, TPMI_DH_OBJECT objectHandle, TPMI_DH_OBJECT parentHandle, TSS2L_SYS_AUTH_COMMAND const *cmdAuthsArray, const TPM2B_AUTH *newAuth, TPM2B_PRIVATE *outPrivate, TSS2L_SYS_AUTH_RESPONSE *rspAuthsArray);
functions.description: One-shot helper for TPM2_ObjectChangeAuth. Sends the command and returns the updated private area with new authorization, handling auth sessions.
requirements: sysContext must be a valid, initialized TSS2_SYS_CONTEXT
cmdAuthsArray may be NULL or must have count <= TSS2_SYS_MAX_SESSIONS
newAuth and outPrivate must be valid pointers
rspAuthsArray may be NULL or must have space for up to TSS2_SYS_MAX_SESSIONS responses
objectHandle and parentHandle must be valid TPM handles for this command

functions.name: Tss2_Sys_Duplicate_Prepare
functions.signature: TSS2_RC Tss2_Sys_Duplicate_Prepare(TSS2_SYS_CONTEXT *sysContext, TPMI_DH_OBJECT objectHandle, TPMI_DH_OBJECT newParentHandle, const TPM2B_DATA *encryptionKeyIn, const TPMT_SYM_DEF_OBJECT *symmetricAlg);

requirements: sysContext must be valid and initialized
objectHandle and newParentHandle must be valid object handles
encryptionKeyIn and symmetricAlg, if provided by signature, must point to valid structures
Must be followed by Execute* then the matching Complete

functions.name: Tss2_Sys_Duplicate_Complete

requirements: sysContext must match the earlier Prepare/Execute
encryptionKeyOut, duplicate, and outSymSeed must be valid pointers to receive outputs (as required by use)
Call only after successful Execute* for this command

functions.name: Tss2_Sys_Duplicate
functions.signature: TSS2_RC Tss2_Sys_Duplicate(TSS2_SYS_CONTEXT *sysContext, TPMI_DH_OBJECT objectHandle, TPMI_DH_OBJECT newParentHandle, TSS2L_SYS_AUTH_COMMAND const *cmdAuthsArray, const TPM2B_DATA *encryptionKeyIn, const TPMT_SYM_DEF_OBJECT *symmetricAlg, TPM2B_DATA *encryptionKeyOut, TPM2B_PRIVATE *duplicate, TPM2B_ENCRYPTED_SECRET *outSymSeed, TSS2L_SYS_AUTH_RESPONSE *rspAuthsArray);
functions.description: One-shot helper for TPM2_Duplicate. Duplicates an object for import under a new parent and returns duplicate blob, seed, and optional inner key.
requirements: sysContext must be valid and initialized
cmdAuthsArray may be NULL or must have count <= TSS2_SYS_MAX_SESSIONS
objectHandle and newParentHandle must be valid handles
encryptionKeyIn/symmetricAlg may be NULL depending on scheme; if provided must be valid
encryptionKeyOut, duplicate, outSymSeed must be valid pointers for outputs
rspAuthsArray may be NULL or capable of holding up to TSS2_SYS_MAX_SESSIONS

functions.name: Tss2_Sys_Rewrap_Prepare
functions.signature: TSS2_RC Tss2_Sys_Rewrap_Prepare(TSS2_SYS_CONTEXT *sysContext, TPMI_DH_OBJECT oldParent, TPMI_DH_OBJECT newParent, const TPM2B_PRIVATE *inDuplicate, const TPM2B_NAME *name, const TPM2B_ENCRYPTED_SECRET *inSymSeed);
functions.description: Prepare stage for TPM2_Rewrap. Builds request to rewrap a duplicate blob from one parent to another.
requirements: sysContext must be valid and initialized
oldParent and newParent must be valid object handles
inDuplicate, name, and inSymSeed must point to valid structures
Must be followed by Execute* and corresponding Complete

functions.name: Tss2_Sys_Rewrap_Complete
functions.signature: TSS2_RC Tss2_Sys_Rewrap_Complete(TSS2_SYS_CONTEXT *sysContext, TPM2B_PRIVATE *outDuplicate, TPM2B_ENCRYPTED_SECRET *outSymSeed);

requirements: sysContext must match the prior Prepare/Execute
outDuplicate and outSymSeed must be valid pointers
Call only after successful Execute*

requirements: sysContext must be valid and initialized
cmdAuthsArray may be NULL or count <= TSS2_SYS_MAX_SESSIONS
oldParent/newParent must be valid handles
inDuplicate, name, inSymSeed must be valid pointers
outDuplicate and outSymSeed must be valid pointers

functions.name: Esys_Initialize
functions.signature: TSS2_RC Esys_Initialize(ESYS_CONTEXT **esys_context, TSS2_TCTI_CONTEXT *tcti, TSS2_ABI_VERSION *abiVersion);
functions.description: Create and initialize an ESAPI context for communicating with a TPM via a provided TCTI transport. Typical usage is to call this once to obtain an ESYS_CONTEXT*, then use that context for all subsequent Esys_* calls until Esys_Finalize is called. Details of ownership and lifetime are managed by ESAPI.
requirements: esys_context must be a non-NULL pointer to receive a newly created ESYS_CONTEXT* (callee-allocated).
tcti should be a valid, initialized TCTI context compatible with ESAPI.
The function returns a TSS2_RC status; callers must check for TSS2_RC_SUCCESS before using the context.
Must be called before any other Esys_* function that requires a valid ESYS_CONTEXT.
Thread-safety and reentrancy constraints are unknown from this header.

functions.name: Esys_Finalize
functions.signature: void Esys_Finalize(ESYS_CONTEXT **context);
functions.description: Tear down and free an ESAPI context created with Esys_Initialize. After this call, the ESYS_CONTEXT pointer is no longer valid.
requirements: context must be non-NULL and point to a valid ESYS_CONTEXT* previously returned by Esys_Initialize.
After successful return the pointer referenced by context may be set to NULL by the callee; callers must not use the freed context.
Must not be called concurrently with other operations using the same context.

functions.signature: TSS2_RC Esys_GetTcti(ESYS_CONTEXT *esys_context, TSS2_TCTI_CONTEXT **tcti);

requirements: esys_context must be a valid ESYS_CONTEXT initialized by Esys_Initialize.
tcti must be a non-NULL output pointer to receive the TCTI context pointer.
Callers must check the TSS2_RC return value for success before using the returned TCTI pointer.

functions.name: Esys_GetPollHandles

functions.description: Obtain poll handles from the transport layer for integration with event loops. The handles and count describe descriptors you can poll on for TPM activity.
requirements: esys_context must be a valid ESYS_CONTEXT.
handles must be a non-NULL output pointer; memory ownership and lifetime of returned handles are not documented here (unknown).
count must be a non-NULL output pointer to receive the number of handles.
Callers must check the return code before using outputs.

functions.name: Esys_SetTimeout
functions.signature: TSS2_RC Esys_SetTimeout(ESYS_CONTEXT *esys_context, int32_t timeout);
functions.description: Set the overall ESAPI command timeout on the ESYS context. Typically forwards to TCTI to control blocking behavior for TPM commands.
requirements: esys_context must be a valid ESYS_CONTEXT.
timeout value semantics (units and special values like -1) are not specified here; follow ESAPI/TCTI documentation (unknown from this header).
